faq.question: How do I know which service I need?
faq.answer: You don't — and that's fine. Clients arrive with a problem, not a service: "too few enquiries", "sales keeps losing leads", "staff copy data between spreadsheets by hand". Breaking that into concrete work is our job, not yours. Describe the situation in your own words in any messenger and we will tell you what the solution consists of and what it costs. If it turns out the problem is cheaper to solve than you expected, we will say so.

faq.question: What is the difference between a landing page, a one-page site and a corporate website?
faq.answer: Scope and purpose. A landing page is a single page for one product and one advertising channel; its job is to capture an enquiry right now. A business-card site is a minimum presence: who you are, what you do, how to reach you. A corporate website is a multi-page structure with service sections, case studies and a blog, and it works over the long term for search and for the trust of larger clients. More expensive does not mean better: for a single-product ad campaign, a corporate website is wasted money.

faq.question: Can several services be combined into one project?
faq.answer: That is usually how it goes. A website whose enquiries land in a CRM, plus a Telegram bot that notifies the sales manager, is three items on the list but one project with one team and one deadline. The split into services exists so you can see what the estimate is made of, not so we can sell them separately. A combined estimate is almost always lower than the sum of the parts, because some of the work is shared.

faq.question: What if my problem isn't on this list?
faq.answer: Write to us. The list is what we do regularly and already have estimates for — it is not the limit of what we can do. Unusual work, such as integrating with a rare accounting system, a parser for one specific site, or an internal tool shaped around your process, is estimated the same way, just separately. If it isn't our kind of work we will say so plainly and, where we can, point you to someone better suited.

faq.question: Do you only build from scratch, or work with an existing site too?
faq.answer: Both. Improving an existing product is routine for us: adding payments, speeding up loading, rebuilding the layout for mobile, adding an integration, cleaning up code left by a previous team. We start by looking at what exists and telling you honestly where it is cheaper to improve and where to rebuild. We do not propose rewriting everything for the sake of tidy code.

faq.question: Can we start small and grow later?
faq.answer: Yes, and for most problems that is the smarter route. Launching a first version, watching real users and building on what you learn is cheaper than designing the whole system for six months and discovering half the features were unnecessary. We plan for it in the architecture: so that a client portal can be added to the website later, and payments to the bot, without rewriting everything.

1.question: What kinds of products do you build end to end?
1.answer: We build around business problems: web platforms and CRM, corporate websites and eCommerce, Telegram bots and Mini Apps, mobile apps (from MVP to a full product), AI agents and automation, plus blockchain/web3 solutions and internal tools. We run projects in stages: brief, architecture, build, launch, support.

2.question: Can I order just a website, just a Telegram bot or just an AI agent?
2.answer: Yes. We take on single pieces of work as well as complete products. We will suggest the right format, size up the work and propose a launch plan for your goal.

3.question: Do you build MVPs and fast launches?
3.answer: Yes. An MVP is a common format for us. We help you test a hypothesis quickly, build the core functionality and lay a foundation for growth. An MVP usually takes one to two months — we can be precise about scope and budget after a brief.

4.question: Do you support the project after launch?
4.answer: Yes. We offer ongoing IT support: improvements, updates, monitoring and technical help. You can take it as one-off work or as planned development in agreed stages.

5.question: Can you bring AI agents and automation into a business?
5.answer: Yes. We build AI agents for handling enquiries, assistants and content generation, and we connect automation to your existing services and CRM. We also build blockchain/web3 modules where the project calls for them. Price and timeline follow once the requirements are clear.

6.question: How do you work out the price of a project?
6.answer: We usually start with an audit of the problem: goals, context, competitive landscape and the key user journeys. From there we shape a concept, agree the stages, and give you a budget and a timeline after the brief.

7.question: What does a website, a Telegram bot or an AI agent cost?
7.answer: As a guide: websites and landing pages from {price:80000} (from one week), Telegram bots from {price:50000} (from one week), Mini Apps from {price:100000} (from two weeks), AI agents and automation from {price:100000} (from two weeks). Complex work costs more — we agree the exact figure after the brief.

8.question: Do you work with clients outside your region?
8.answer: Yes. We run projects remotely and work with clients anywhere. We start with a brief, then run the project in stages: analysis → architecture → UX → development → launch → support.
